items.entity: Design domain Ω for the Fig. 1 example (shape and aspect ratio)
items.description: Sec. 2.1 only mentions 'the full design domain Ω' and says 'Fig. 1 summarizes the principle of TO'. The shape and proportions of the domain appear only in the figure. The only size anywhere in the paper is the 64x64 dataset image (Sec. 4.1), and the text never says Fig. 1 is a dataset sample. The problem is implied to be 2D (Sec. 4.1; 3D is listed as future work in Sec. 5.3).
readings: Square domain, length:height = 1:1 (matches the 64x64 dataset images)

items.description: No mesh is given for Fig. 1. Sec. 2.1 only mentions 'every element of the mesh' and loads/BCs 'applied on the nodes'. Sec. 4.1 gives 64x64 images, but it also says the load channels give a value to 'every node'. So it is unclear whether 64x64 counts elements or nodes, and whether Fig. 1 uses this grid at all.
readings: 63 x 63 elements (64 x 64 nodes, one image pixel per node)
A different resolution used only for the illustration, e.g. 32 x 32 or 128 x 128 elements

items.entity: Displacement boundary conditions (which nodes/edges are supported)
items.description: Sec. 2.1 only mentions 'a set of displacement boundary conditions ... applied on the nodes'. Where the supports are in Fig. 1 is shown only in the drawing. The 42 + 5 dataset BC scenarios (Sec. 4.1) are never described. The Fig. 2 caption says BCs are drawn as colored lines (edge segments) and dots (single nodes), so their extent can only be read from the figures.
readings: Entire left edge plus the bottom-right corner node (x = L, y = 0)
Bottom-left and bottom-right corner nodes only (x = 0 and x = L at y = 0)
Part of an edge, e.g. the lower half of the left edge (x = 0, 0 ≤ y ≤ 0.5H)

items.entity: Constrained degrees of freedom at the supports
items.description: The text never says whether supported nodes are fixed in x, in y, or in both. The Fig. 2 caption says BCs are drawn with color lines and dots, which suggests different constraint types are color-coded. The type can therefore only be read from the figures.
readings: Fully clamped: u_x = u_y = 0 at all supported nodes
Rollers: only the displacement normal to the edge is fixed
Mixed: one pinned support (u_x = u_y = 0) and one roller (u_y = 0 only)
Symmetry/MBB type: an edge with u_x = 0 only plus one point with u_y = 0 only

items.description: Sec. 2.1 only says loads are 'applied on the nodes of the domain' (so possibly not on the boundary). For the dataset, Sec. 4.1 says loads go on randomly selected unconstrained boundary nodes. The Fig. 1 load location is shown only by the arrow in the figure.
readings: Mid-height of the right edge (x = L, y = 0.5H)
Mid-span of the top edge (x = 0.5L, y = H)
Mid-span of the bottom edge (x = 0.5L, y = 0)

items.entity: Number of nodal forces and load cases
items.description: Sec. 2.1 speaks of 'a set of ... loads' (plural) on the nodes, and Sec. 4.1 says 'the loads are applied on unconstrained nodes'. The Fig. 1 caption ('set of load') and the Fig. 2 caption ('the load applied, represented with an arrow') use the singular. The text does not say how many forces act in Fig. 1, or whether several forces would form one load case or separate ones.
readings: Two concentrated nodal forces acting together in one load case
Two nodal forces treated as separate load cases (compliances summed)
A force spread over a few adjacent boundary nodes

items.description: No direction is given for Fig. 1; it is shown only by an arrow. Dataset loads (Sec. 4.1) use angles in [0, π] in steps of π/6, but the reference axis and the angle sense (y up vs. image y down) are not defined. For a single load, reversing its sign does not change the layout. However, the y-up/y-down ambiguity turns θ into π − θ.

No force value appears in Sec. 2.1, the Fig. 1 caption, or Sec. 4.1 (the load channels store force values, but none are stated). For a single load this only scales compliance (∝ |F|²). If there are several loads, their ratio would also matter.

The Fig. 1 caption mentions 'a given ... volume fraction', but the text gives no value; it may be printed in the figure or not shown at all. The dataset (Sec. 4.1) draws it from [0.3, 0.5] in steps of 0.02.

The text never mentions passive elements for this setup. The load-violation metric (Sec. 4.2) requires material where loads act, and some codes enforce that with passive solid elements, but nothing says the SIMP setup does this. A non-rectangular domain shown in Fig. 1 would also need passive voids.
readings: None: the whole rectangular domain is designable
A small passive solid patch (about 1–2 elements) at each load point
Passive solid elements at both the load and support nodes
A passive void region that makes the domain non-rectangular (e.g. L-shaped)

items.description: No material constants are given anywhere. Sec. 2.1 describes SIMP only in general terms.

Neither Poisson's ratio nor the 2D elasticity state is stated. Only a 2D problem is implied (64x64 images and the 2D stress/strain components in Sec. 4.1). These choices change the form of the constitutive matrix, not just its scale.
Sec. 2.1 only says the penalization is used 'with p > 1'. Neither the value for Fig. 1 nor the one used in ToPy for the ground truth (Sec. 4.1) is given.

Sec. 2.1 mentions filters only in general ('Other techniques ... include filters'). Sec. 3.2 says the ground truth may be sub-optimal because of the penalization factor and filters, which implies a filter was used, but its type and radius are never given.
readings: Sensitivity or density filter, r_min = 3 elements

items.entity: Optimizer, initial design, void stiffness and stopping criterion
items.description: Sec. 2.1 calls SIMP gradient-based and notes it is non-convex and tends to converge to local optima. Sec. 4.1 names ToPy for the dataset. But the update scheme, move limit, starting densities, minimum (void) stiffness and convergence tolerance are never given, and for a non-convex problem these can change the converged layout.
readings: OC update, move limit 0.2, uniform start at the volume fraction, Emin = 1e-9·E, stop when the maximum density change < 0.01
MMA update with the same start and tolerance
OC with a fixed budget of 100 iterations

items.entity: Conversion of SIMP densities to the black-and-white result
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says the optimal topology is stored as a 'black and white image', but SIMP produces gray densities and no thresholding or projection step is described. How the Fig. 1 result was made binary, if it was, is unknown.
readings: Threshold chosen so the binary design meets the prescribed volume fraction exactly

items.entity: Objective function of the Fig. 1 example
items.description: Sec. 2.1 ('an objective function, such as mechanical compliance') and the Fig. 1 caption ('objectives such as compliance') give compliance only as an example. They do not state it as the objective actually used in Fig. 1.
readings: Minimum compliance with a volume constraint (single load case)
Another objective (e.g. stress-based), which a minimum-compliance solver could not reproduce
